transcript:
Meeting header: Date: 2027-06-08 14:00 UTC | Duration: 62 minutes | Location: Zoom
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Arjun Patel (Redwood SE), Elena Park (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Cerulean SA), Rajiv Banerjee (CTO), Nora Li (Platform Eng), Tom Geller (Security)

Summary: quick check on marketplace listing artifacts, ensure KMS compatibility for customer-managed keys in GovCloud/on-prem, and plan a UAT with prod-like egress/NAT and HB (heartbeat) probes.

[00:00:10] Maya: hey everyone thanks for joining, we wanted to run through the listing checklist and the bits that usually trip partners up, and then get into the k‑m‑s flow for your private deployments.
[00:00:36] Lena: yeah thanks, we have a tight window to get the listing in before our Q3 launch, so focusing on the packaging and the KMS part is critical.
[00:01:05] Arjun: great — quick intro from our side, I'm Arjun (SE), will handle the deployment and perf bits, Elena's on packaging / helm. Maya is your AE and will own next steps.
[00:01:32] Rajiv: sounds good. high level, we run a hybrid: main customers in GovCloud, some on-prem instances for regulated customers. Want to understand if Redwood's marketplace artifact supports onprem connectors with our HSM-backed keys.
[00:02:03] Arjun: yes — we have a couple of patterns. For GovCloud we usually do a terraform + helm combo and reference the customer KMS key via env var or secret. For air‑gapped/ on prem we recommend the connector package that talks to a customer KMS via a local proxy; there's also an HSM plugin we can wire up.
[00:02:40] Nora: can you clarify the flow — do you push encrypted model shards to the node and then the key unwrap happens locally? there's a couple approaches and we need to match our compliance team.
[00:03:05] Arjun: right, two main flows: 1) key unwrap with KMS on first boot, then store unwrapped in memory only, or 2) use pass‑through where the runtime requests signed tokens for decryption on the fly. Pass‑through is lower blast radius but higher latency.
[00:03:34] Tom: security perspective, we prefer minimal persistent key material and HSM-backed attestation — does Redwood support attestation via PKCS#11 or cloud HSM?
[00:03:58] Elena: we have a PKCS#11 adapter in our onprem connector; it is supported but the docs are a little rough, we'll share the integration notes.
[00:04:22] Maya: quick note, we'll post the adapter doc link after the call — it's currently internal but we can sanitize for your security team.
[00:04:45] [00:05:12] Lena: on listing, what does the marketplace manifest require? required fields, packaging, and do you accept operator packages vs helm charts?
[00:05:34] Elena: we accept both, but the marketplace portal prefers OCI image + Helm chart. If you provide an Operator bundle we can wrap it into a helm-compatible wrapper for listing. The manifest needs: listing metadata, deployment templates, licensing text, and a test manifest for the UAT account.
[00:06:01] Rajiv: how strict is the network model for UAT? we need prod‑like egress and NAT to simulate telemetry to our monitoring.
[00:06:28] Arjun: for UAT we ask for a prod‑like VPC with NAT gateway or egress proxy. We run a short smoke suite and then a perf run for 30 minutes to see cold start/kv cache behavior.
[00:06:55] Nora: cold start is a big one for us, especially with quantized models. can you repro quantized perf in your benchmarks?
[00:07:20] Arjun: yes, we'll run a quantized path that mirrors your token length distribution. Ask you to share a 2‑hour sample trace of typical requests (anonymized).
[00:07:47] Lena: we can do that, will scrub PII.
[00:08:10] [00:08:45] Tom: about audits — we need to ensure audit logs are available from the connector and that they meet our retention policy. does Redwood's connector emit structured audit events?
[00:09:05] Elena: yes, connector emits JSON audit logs with request id, model id, user id (hashed) and outcome. retention for the listing default is 90 days but can be configured to ship to your SIEM.
[00:09:32] Rajiv: good, we will want a S3 sink to our account. is cross‑account S3 supported for logs?
[00:09:58] Arjun: yes we support cross‑account S3 delivery; we'll provide the iam role trust policy you need to create.
[00:10:20] [00:10:55] Maya: quick pause — wanted to call out a common marketplace rejection: missing test manifest or insufficient network docs. We're going to share a checklist so you can tick boxes before upload.
[00:11:18] Lena: appreciated. what about dependency scanning for the operator chart? the listing requires SBOM/ vulnerability scan.
[00:11:40] Elena: we require an SBOM and a scan report; if you don't have one we can accept an attestation and run a scan in our pipeline but it may delay listing.
[00:12:02] Nora: one more on KMS — in GovCloud we have a dedicated KMS and customer‑managed keys; do you support BYOK (bring your own key) and the KMS key ARN mapping?
[00:12:29] Arjun: yes BYOK is supported. For BYOK we require the key ARN and a test policy that allows Decrypt: our runtime assumed role/principal. We'll send a sample policy.
[00:12:50] [00:13:15] Tom: on compliance, can we get a list of data flows? our legal wants a diagram that shows where tokens and logs go.
[00:13:38] Maya: we'll attach the standard flow diagram and annotate the marketplace variant and the on‑prem variant.
[00:13:54] [00:14:22] Rajiv: curious about the packaging size — is there a max image size or layer limit for the marketplace? we have model artifacts that are 6‑8GB each.
[00:14:47] Elena: marketplace accepts OCI images up to 20GB, but we usually recommend storing model shards in an external object store and referencing them from the chart to keep listings small. For govcloud, ensure your object store is accessible from UAT with signed URLs.
[00:15:14] [00:15:40] Lena: for onprem installs, do you support pulling from a private registry behind a firewall?
[00:15:59] Arjun: yes — private registries and air‑gapped registries are supported. We provide a registry mirror pattern in our packaging docs.
[00:16:20] [00:16:44] Maya: switching to UAT timeline — you're aiming for last week of June for a sandbox run?
[00:16:58] Lena: yes, ideal is last week of June, but we can stretch into the first week of July if needed.
[00:17:21] Arjun: operationally we need about 5 business days after we receive the manifest + KMS test ARNs to provision and validate. If you give us the artifacts by June 10 we can hit the end of June window.
[00:17:49] [00:18:12] Nora: ok will prioritize. Question on the benchmark: do you instrument and show per‑token latency and KV cache hit ratios?
[00:18:34] Arjun: yes results will include p50/p95/p99 per token, tokens per second, and kv cache hit rate. We'll also show end to end for small and large payloads.
[00:18:58] [00:19:20] Elena: also will include docker image manifest checklist and a sample values.yaml for helm.
[00:19:43] Rajiv: any gotchas for private deployments with customer KMS and network egress? we want to avoid an open egress path.
[00:20:07] Arjun: you can use VPC endpoints and a private S3 endpoint for model shards; for telemetry, we support a push model to your SIEM and also an optional relay in your VPC so no public egress needed.
[00:20:35] [00:20:58] Tom: does Redwood's runtime support FIPS mode for crypto? we require FIPS‑validated stacks in some customers.
[00:21:18] Elena: we have a FIPS mode on our connector build; requires a specific kernel and libc. We'll share the compatibility matrix.
[00:21:45] [00:22:10] Maya: ok let's talk about the listing manifest fields — Elena, can you walk through the minimal manifest?
[00:22:30] Elena: sure — fields: display name, short/long descr, tags, support contacts, licensing (OSS or commercial), deployment templates, test manifest (k8s namespace + test user), required instance types, recommended model quantizations, and a compliance section where you list SOC2/ISO links and SBOM.
[00:23:05] [00:23:30] Lena: for the compliance section, do you accept a link to our auditor's report? we might need to redact details.
[00:23:52] Maya: yes link is fine; we'll store it with restricted access and our marketplace team will only pull metadata.
[00:24:10] [00:24:35] Rajiv: technical question — when using KV cache across shards, is cache warming required per node? will the cache be shared or local?
[00:24:58] Arjun: currently cache is local to the runtime instance. For distributed cache we have a shared layer in our dedicated offering but not for marketplace single installs. Warming strategies: use a preheat script in the test manifest to prime cache.
[00:25:27] [00:25:52] Nora: can the preheat use an anonymized corpus?
[00:26:10] Arjun: yes, just provide us the script and sample payload.
[00:26:30] [00:26:55] Elena: also note that quantized models may have different warmup characteristics; will document recommended warmup tokens.
[00:27:20] [00:27:46] Maya: quick recap of immediate actions: we'll share the packaging checklist, PKCS#11 adapter doc (sanitized), sample IAM policy for BYOK, and a template values.yaml. Arjun will run a perf pass on an anonymized sample if you provide it.
[00:28:12] Lena: good. also want to confirm pricing visibility in the listing — do you show per‑token estimates?
[00:28:36] Maya: marketplace listing can include recommended pricing, but actual runtime billing is handled outside the marketplace in your contract; we can suggest per‑token guidance for customers.
[00:28:58] [00:29:20] Rajiv: any limitations with operator lifecycle upgrades via marketplace? we need to test zero downtime upgrades.
[00:29:45] Elena: lifecycle best practice is to use helm controlled hooks and readiness probes; we'll include an upgrade test in the test manifest. Zero downtime is achievable but depends on model load and shard count.
[00:30:10] [00:30:33] Tom: last thing for me — can you provide a concise list of evidence items for our compliance pack? auditor wants to see configuration, role policy, and logs mapping.
[00:30:58] Maya: yes we'll produce an evidence template for the marketplace/onprem variants.
[00:31:20] [00:31:45] Lena: okay any blockers we should be aware of?
[00:31:58] Arjun: only blocker might be if KMS policy cannot be modified for our test principal — we can do a more limited smoke without key modification but full perf requires decrypt permission.
[00:32:22] Nora: we should be able to provide the policy.
[00:32:40] [00:33:05] Elena: small note — registry mirroring for airgapped installs needs image rewrite tool; we'll add that to the checklist.
[00:33:30] Rajiv: timeline recap? artifacts by June 10, Redwood runs perf and test by June 14, UAT end of June or first week July.
[00:33:55] Maya: correct. we'll follow up with calendar invites for a 1 hour UAT kickoff once we validate artifacts.
[00:34:20] [00:34:45] Lena: thanks everyone, this was useful.
[00:35:00] Maya: thanks all — we'll send links and the manifest template.

(Notes: small transcription errors present; some speaker overlaps indicated. Links promised: packaging checklist (link to internal doc), PKCS#11 adapter doc (sanitized), sample IAM policy for BYOK.)
